status: Row-window input and resumable run retention now detach and charge rows; complete vector/task/backend/output ownership remains open
contract: WindowRowBuffer detaches supported scanner data before scanner advance, admits retained row references and directories, and preserves incremental serialized-size tracking.

Ordinary row-window execution retains the input scope through yielded output. Resumable execution retains it through evaluation, state serialization and awaited spill writes. Completion, failure and early return dispose the scope.
Flush transfers the current run array into the run directory and allocates a new current array, avoiding splice copying. Serialized run-size accounting resets without releasing retained earlier runs.
Restored rows are detached and admitted when attached to their retained row/run buffer. Existing state parsing and initial run chunk construction still need pre-allocation admission.
Standalone internal collection calls without a supplied parent scope release reservations when returning plain rows to their caller; public execution supplies the parent scope.

cases: Ordinary, checkpoint and spill window execution preserve earlier rows when a scanner repeatedly mutates and yields one object.
Detached byte views survive scanner buffer mutation; input reservations remain live while streaming output is suspended, and early return preserves an unrelated sibling reservation.
16 KiB admission rejects growing input before all 100 rows are scanned, for ordinary and spill execution, closing the scanner and releasing reservations.
A pending asynchronous spill write keeps at least the detached input payload reserved until the write settles; afterward only the sibling reservation remains.

HTTP 206 and ignored-Range 200 real Brotli fixtures now include checkpoint window execution, alongside ordinary window execution; the same route passes native local Worker R2 under 64/128 MiB shared pools and 2 MiB query caps.
The serialized-budget error test retains its one-byte serialized limit and expected metric, with an explicit independent 64 KiB allocation cap.

limits: Non-resumable vector-window batch capture and delegated window task outputs still require ownership integration. These real-fixture tests intentionally exercise the row scanner fallback.

Window backend copied rows, sort/partition structures, computed values, accumulated returned rows, checkpoint encoding, initial state parsing/chunking and source adapter backing remain partially or wholly unadmitted.
Spill configuration does not guarantee external streaming execution: retained runs still consume admitted memory and reject on exhaustion.
The established detachable-data contract excludes cycles, accessors and unsupported custom prototypes. No CPU throughput speedup or whole-runtime heap bound is claimed.
Final release gates and the broader audit remain open.
